name: ObjectStore
tagline: Pioneering C++/Java object database that maps persistent objects into virtual memory; now sold by IgniteTech.
description: ObjectStore is a commercial object database created in 1988 by Object Design, Inc., a company founded by former Symbolics engineers including Dan Weinreb. Its signature idea is transparent persistence for C++: objects are allocated in the database through an overloaded operator new, database pages are memory-mapped on demand when a pointer is first dereferenced, and pointers are swizzled so the same database works across platforms, making persistent objects behave like ordinary in-memory ones; Java support followed later. Progress Software acquired the product in 2002, and in 2013 it moved to an ESW Capital company; today IgniteTech sells and supports it as 'ObjectStore AI'. It still runs inside long-lived telecom, finance, travel and GIS systems, but it is a legacy choice for new projects.
statusNote: Sold and supported by IgniteTech (ESW Capital) since Progress divested it in 2013; no public roadmap or recent release notes.
strengths: Persistent C++ objects behave like ordinary in-memory objects
Page-level memory mapping makes pointer navigation extremely fast
Decades of production use in telecom, finance and GIS
weaknesses: Closed, expensive and owned by a vendor focused on maintaining legacy software
Tight coupling between application classes and the database schema
Small and shrinking pool of developers who know it
useCases: Maintaining existing C++ or Java systems built on ObjectStore
Navigation-heavy object graphs where pointer chasing dominates
